newsitem.title: CHINA: China to ease controls on paper imports.
newsitem.headline: China to ease controls on paper imports.

text.p: China is planning to relax restrictions on paper processing plants that require firms importing paper for export products to ensure that their total output is exported, the Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The restrictions, passed this year to crack down on paper smuggling, had been effective in curbing smuggling and had sent the official figures for paper imports soaring, said the newspaper, which is published by the official China Daily.
Under the restrictions, the plants could not even use their own products as packing materials, it said but gave no details.
But the rules had also upset Hong Kong companies and would be relaxed, the newspaper quoted An Min, assistant minister of foreign trade and economic cooperation, as saying.
In future plants that imported paper would be required to attach distinct trademarks to their paper products before selling them, An said.
He gave no other details of the new rules or when they would be implemented.
